G-O.acceptance_policy: Amended 26 July 2026, before any test article was opened. Order per attempt: native tool call; else whole-document content JSON, accepting BOTH the {"quotes": [...]} envelope and a bare array, with the single unterminated-string repair; else PER-ENTRY recovery — individual entries extracted and validated against the same pydantic schema, recovered/dropped counts recorded. Per-entry runs only after every whole-document path fails, so articles those paths already accept are untouched and development results cannot move (pinned by regression test).

H.multiplicity_control: The set is frozen in full before the test split is touched and EVERY variant is reported, winner or not. The primary contrast (G-C − Q on detection F1) is fixed and does not move to whichever variant wins on test. The earlier "at most one additional hybrid row" limit was a page-budget heuristic, not a safeguard, and was lifted 26 July 2026 on the ground that the paper asks whether and how AI improves this pipeline — a question a single combination cannot answer. What protects against multiplicity is predeclaration and complete reporting, not a small count.

early_cut_criterion.criterion_text: if the open-weight detector fails the offset-recovery smoke test (§4.3) or is clearly dominated on development, cut to one generative system
early_cut_criterion.decision: KEEP G-O (ollama_gemma4-26b-mlx). Recorded 2026-07-26 by the author.
evidence: Objective trigger not met: the offset-recovery smoke test is the criterion's only measurable arm, and G-O passed it — 10/10 on Mentz (18 July 2026) and 85/85 across the full development set (22 July 2026) — against a >10% failure floor.

The 'clearly dominated' arm is a judgement clause whose stated purpose was calendar and page-budget relief, not a claim that a weaker detector is uninformative. Neither pressure applies: the development runs are complete and already paid for.

G-O is not dominated uniformly but asymmetrically, which is itself a result: 17/18 recall on unmarked block quotations (the stratum where the M baseline scores 0/18) against 5/16 on curly-single spans, where it is the weakest system in the matrix.

G-O is the only system carrying the open-weight reproducibility and cost axis. Cutting it would remove the paper's ability to say whether the method is runnable without commercial API access, which is part of the stated contribution.
The open/closed elicitation difference is only observable with G-O present: it made no native tool call on any of the four development articles despite tool-calling being its frozen mechanism.
early_cut_criterion.framing_note: The paper's question is whether open-weight and frontier models improve on existing quotation-detection methods. Reporting both models is the evaluation; a self-imposed reduction rule adopted for workload control is not a reason to withhold a completed, valid result. The criterion is recorded here as set aside deliberately, with reasons, rather than silently unapplied.
early_cut_criterion.gate_note: The plan set this gate at 24 July; the decision was recorded on 26 July, two days late, by which point the full development metrics existed. Disclosed rather than back-dated: the "clearly dominated" judgement was therefore made with more information than the gate envisaged.

statistics.primary_contrast: G-C minus Q on detection F1, article-level paired bootstrap; end-to-end F1 secondary.
statistics.note: Predeclared 2026-07-26, before any test article was opened. Six systems yield 15 pairwise contrasts across several metrics; naming the primary contrast in advance forecloses selection after the fact. Every other comparison is estimation, reported with intervals and not as a test.
statistics.paired_seed: derived from each pair's identity (crc32 of the tag pair), not its enumeration index, so intervals do not move when the system set changes.
statistics.supplementary: exact paired sign test on per-article differences, plus the full per-article difference table (n=12 on test).
